headline: RIO TINTO HALTS OYU TOLGOI UNDERGROUND — Seismic Event Injures Workers at World's 4th-Largest Copper Mine
snippet: Rio Tinto paused all underground operations at its Oyu Tolgoi copper-gold mine in Mongolia on October 29 after a seismic event along a rock fault zone injured an estimated three to fifteen workers (sources disagree on the count); no fatalities have been reported and a safety review is underway with no restart timeline confirmed. At annualised capacity of 450,000 tonnes of copper per year — with Rio holding a 66% stake — any extended halt would represent a significant supply disruption in an already tight global copper market. The suspension adds fresh upside risk to copper prices at a time when the Yangshan import premium is already at a 13-year high.

headline: AGNICO EAGLE Q3: $852M FREE CASH FLOW, NET INCOME +28% — Beats Estimates as Gold Tests $4,000
snippet: Agnico Eagle (TSX/NYSE: AEM) reported Q3 2026 net income of US$1.35 billion (US$2.67/share), up 28% year-over-year, with adjusted EPS of US$2.62 beating the consensus estimate of US$2.51. Free cash flow hit a record US$852 million, and US$478 million was returned to shareholders through dividends and buybacks. Gold production of 814,012 ounces was down 6% primarily due to lower output at Canadian Malartic and Meadowbank; the company remains on track to meet the lower end of annual production guidance and the upper end of cost guidance. After quarter-end, Agnico raised its revolving credit facility to US$3 billion and confirmed Hope Bay construction is on schedule.

headline: TOP 50 MINERS SHED $264B AS GOLD TRADE UNWINDS — Lithium Names Exit Rankings, Copper Producers Hold Firm
snippet: Mining.com's quarterly ranking of the world's 50 largest miners by market cap shows a combined loss of approximately US$264 billion as gold's 25% decline from its January 2026 all-time high above US$5,300 has hammered precious metals producers; senior gold miners including Newmont and Kinross are trading at 9–15x forward earnings while copper names Freeport and Southern Copper hold at 21–24x. The lithium sector has shrunk to just three companies in the top 50 from six at the 2022 peak, reflecting continued price weakness in battery-grade carbonate. BHP remains the world's most valuable miner at roughly US$214 billion, while the sector total has retreated from the US$2.33 trillion peak reached at end of March 2026.

headline: ZIMBABWE REJECTS LITHIUM DELAY PLEA — January 2027 Concentrate Export Ban Stands; Arcadia and Bikita Face Crunch
snippet: Zimbabwe's Mines Minister Polite Kambamura officially rejected the Lithium Producers Association's request for a six-month delay to the country's January 1, 2027 ban on lithium concentrate exports, saying companies had been given sufficient time to build local processing facilities. Producers including Arcadia (Prospect Resources), Bikita Minerals, and Zulu Lithium face a hard deadline in 63 days; those without commissioned processing plants would be forced to halt concentrate shipments — a move that could temporarily remove a meaningful chunk of African lithium supply from global markets. Zimbabwe was Africa's largest lithium producer in 2025 with output topping US$2.15 billion in the first nine months of this year.

headline: MALAYSIA BREAKS RAW RARE EARTH BAN FOR US RESEARCH — DTEC Wins 700-Tonne Carbonate Export Permit
snippet: Malaysia's Natural Resources Ministry approved DTEC Mineral and Metal Technology's application to export up to 700 metric tonnes of rare-earth carbonate from Perak state to the United States for research purposes, with an initial 30-tonne shipment expected imminently — the first such export since Malaysia banned raw rare earth exports in 2024. The approval follows Malaysia's release of conditional research-export guidelines and comes as DTEC, which is 51% US-owned, has secured an expression of US Export-Import Bank support for up to US$650 million for a planned Malaysian rare earth refinery. The permit is a research exemption, not a reversal of the raw export ban, but signals a deepening US-Malaysia critical minerals partnership.

headline: ENCORE ENERGY'S DEWEY-BURDOCK URANIUM UNLOCKS STATE PERMITTING — Public Comment Opens After 14-Year Halt in South Dakota
snippet: A public comment period has opened for state-level water and environmental permits at enCore Energy's (TSXV: EU / NASDAQ: EU) Dewey-Burdock in-situ recovery uranium project in South Dakota's Black Hills region, marking the first meaningful state permitting activity in more than 14 years after litigation and water rights disputes repeatedly stalled progress. Federal permitting was completed in June 2026 when the NRC issued a 20-year license renewal and the BLM authorized site infrastructure. State approval of water permits remains the final regulatory bottleneck before enCore can advance toward construction at what would be one of the only licensed uranium ISR operations in South Dakota.

headline: COPPER BOUNCES AS MARKETS STABILIZE — Oyu Tolgoi Halt Adds Supply Risk on Top of Record Yangshan Premium
snippet: LME three-month copper rebounded toward US$14,400 per tonne on October 30 as equity markets found footing after the week's rate-hike-driven selloff and LME warehouse inventories stabilised. Separately, the seismic halt at Rio Tinto's Oyu Tolgoi — which accounts for roughly 450,000 tonnes annualised copper production — has added an unplanned supply risk premium to the market. SMM's October 30 morning note flagged that US economic resilience is keeping December rate-hike odds above 80%, which continues to cap copper's upside, while the Yangshan spot premium to LME at US$205/t remains near a 13-year high — an indicator that Chinese physical demand is absorbing available supply.

headline: GOLD IS TESTING $4,000 — THESE 10 MINING STOCKS NOW TRADE AT MULTI-YEAR DISCOUNTS TO BULLION
snippet: An Investing.com analysis identifies ten gold and silver producers — including Newmont, Agnico Eagle, First Majestic, Pan American Silver, and Coeur Mining — trading at RSI readings of 28–33 and price-to-NAV multiples well below their five-year averages as gold tests the critical US$4,000 support level. The piece argues the current equity selloff has overshot the spot metal's decline: spot gold is down roughly 25% from January highs while the GDX miners ETF has dropped approximately 29%, creating a relative-value setup that has historically preceded sharp sector recoveries. The key variable: whether the Fed delivers the priced-in December hike and gold holds US$3,900, or if a deeper reset toward US$3,600 needs to be absorbed first.

headline: RECORD CENTRAL BANK GOLD BUYING CAN'T LIFT MINING STOCKS — Analysts Cite Cost Inflation, Production Misses as Culprits
snippet: A Crux Investor analysis examines why gold miners have underperformed even the already-declining spot metal in 2026 — GDX down ~29% versus gold down ~25% from January highs — despite official-sector demand running at record levels, with the PBOC adding gold for 21 consecutive months and central bank purchases outpacing ETF outflows six-to-one. The piece attributes the disconnect to three compounding headwinds: cost inflation lifting industry-wide AISC toward US$1,700/oz in many cases, a wave of Q3 production disappointments (Kinross revenues missed by US$190 million, multiple producers guided lower), and rate hike expectations suppressing the entire precious metals complex. Bank of America has separately flagged that miners are trading at a 19% discount to an already-corrected spot price — a historically rare gap.

headline: MALAYSIA'S KELANTAN STATE COMMITS TO RARE EARTH MINING IN 2027 — Two Local Companies Cleared as Kedah Pushes for Federal Policy
snippet: Kelantan state expects two locally owned companies to commence rare earth element mining operations in 2027, adding a second state-level mining commitment alongside Perak's DTEC export approval announced this week. Neighboring Kedah state simultaneously pressed the federal government for a clearer national rare earth industry policy framework. The dual state-level push comes as Malaysia navigates a delicate balance: the 2024 ban on raw rare earth exports remains in effect, yet both the US and Japan are actively courting Malaysian REE supply for critical minerals supply chain diversification. Malaysia holds the second-largest rare earth deposits in Asia after China, a position its domestic processors have yet to fully monetise.
